title: PhenObs: is peak flowering of medicinal species predictable across gardens (monitoring calendar)?
question: For medicinal species monitored in >=3 botanical gardens, how much of peak-flowering-day variance is species identity vs garden vs year, and does a species-mean model beat a grand-mean baseline in leave-one-garden-out prediction?
hypothesis: Species explains most variance; species-mean beats grand mean (lower MAE); adding a garden offset improves further. Gardens are not wild populations.
method: variance components via OLS sums of squares; leave-one-garden-out CV
finding: Species identity explains 79% of peak-flowering variance (garden 4%, year 0.4%). Leave-one-garden-out MAE: grand mean 35.5 d, species mean 15.4 d, +garden offset 14.1 d. Published C-score/intensity link: rho=0.14, p=0.025 (weak, same direction). Garden plants, not wild populations: monitoring-window suggestion only.

published_relation_check.description: competitive ability (CSR C-score) vs mean maximum flowering intensity, all species
